topics.answer: Hi! I'm Carlos, an iOS developer based in Coimbra, Portugal. Ask me anything about my work, my apps or my skills.
Thanks for stopping by! If you'd like to talk, email me at carlosanielrf@gmail.com.
You can ask about my current job at Bosch, my previous work, Periplum (my own app), my tech stack, architecture, testing, education, languages, or how to contact me.

I'm an iOS developer with 7 years shipping to the App Store. I've worked on a B2B marketplace launched in 20 countries, a Portuguese C2C marketplace, and, for the last five years at Bosch, the apps that control home heating from your phone. On my own time I built Periplum, my own iOS app, solo from first commit to store listing.

questions: How many years of experience do you have?
How long have you been an iOS developer?
topics.answer: 7 years as an iOS developer (since January 2019), plus a few months before that as a web developer, starting in September 2018.

questions: What do you do at the moment?
topics.answer: I'm an iOS developer at Bosch Thermotechnology in Aveiro, since July 2021. I develop and maintain the connected-heating apps for four Bosch brands.

questions: Which apps do you work on at Bosch?
What Bosch apps have you built?
Tell me about Vulcano Connect and IVT Anywhere
topics.answer: HomeCom Easy, MyBuderus, Vulcano Connect and IVT Anywhere. They let people control their home heating from their phone, and all four ship from one shared iOS codebase.

questions: How do you handle four brands in one codebase?
Tell me about the shared codebase
topics.answer: The four Bosch brands ship from a single iOS codebase. A big part of the job is adapting one interface to a whole catalogue of appliance types and generations, for users spread across ages, countries and languages.

questions: How does the app talk to the appliance?
topics.answer: Yes. I work on the app-to-appliance integration, where software has to talk to a physical heating appliance and get it right every time. Customers feel that link as comfort at home, so it gets the same scrutiny as anything on screen.

questions: Do you have machine learning experience?
topics.answer: At Bosch I tested a Core ML model for on-device anomaly detection, reading faults in an appliance from its heating and cooling data.

questions: Where did you work before Bosch?
topics.answer: Before Bosch I was at Appsconcept (IPN, Coimbra): first as a web developer from September 2018, then as an iOS developer from January 2019 to July 2021.

questions: Tell me about Agriaffaires and Truckscorner
What apps did you build from scratch?
topics.answer: At Appsconcept I built a B2B marketplace from scratch, launched in 20 countries as three branded apps: MachineryZone, Agriaffaires and Truckscorner. That's three business models over one shared codebase, and all three held above 3.3★ in France, the primary market.

questions: Tell me about the app rating improvement
Have you improved an app's rating?
topics.answer: I maintained CustoJusto, a Portuguese C2C marketplace. By clearing the defects its reviews kept naming, the App Store rating went up two stars, to 4.5★.

questions: Have you worked with React or Angular?
topics.answer: I started as a web developer (2018–2019), working on a big-data dashboard in React and Angular that generated client-tailored charts. That's where I learned how much analytics shapes a product. I also worked on an on-site AR preview tool for a construction firm.
I worked on an on-site preview tool for a construction firm: physical markers let clients see unbuilt foundations and structures through the camera.

questions: Tell me about your own app
Have you built an app alone?
topics.answer: Periplum is my own iOS app, live on the App Store in Portugal, Spain, France and Italy. I did everything solo: design, architecture, code, release and store listing.

SwiftUI and SwiftData on iOS 18, Swift 6 strict concurrency, with domain logic isolated in a local Swift package. It has widgets for the Home Screen, Lock Screen and Control Center, App Intents for Shortcuts and Siri, StoreKit 2 purchases with entitlement verification, 6 locales via String Catalogs, and Firebase Auth, Analytics and Crashlytics.

questions: Can I see your apps on the App Store?
Where can I download your apps?
topics.answer: Here's everything I've shipped or maintained. The Bosch apps and Periplum are current; CustoJusto and the B2B marketplace apps were 2019–2021.

Swift and SwiftUI daily, with solid UIKit experience too. I've also worked with RxSwift, SwiftData, WidgetKit, App Intents, MapKit, PDFKit, StoreKit 2, Core ML and Swift Concurrency, on iPhone and iPad.
Yes. Periplum runs on Swift 6 strict concurrency, and I use Swift Concurrency in my day-to-day work.

questions: Which programming languages do you know?
topics.answer: Swift mainly, plus Kotlin Multiplatform and JavaScript.

questions: How do you structure an app?
topics.answer: MVVM, MVP, MVC and VIPER, used where they earn their keep. For dependencies: SPM, CocoaPods and Carthage. In Periplum I keep the domain logic in a local Swift package, separate from the UI.

questions: How do you test your apps?
topics.answer: Yes. Periplum has 449 automated tests with Swift Testing, run on every push through CI. At Bosch I test REST endpoints against product requirements every release, catching contract drift before it reaches customers.
I work with REST API design and Swagger, and I test API contracts before release, not after, so drift gets caught before customers see it.

questions: Which CI tools do you use?
topics.answer: GitHub Actions, Jenkins and Travis CI, with TestFlight for beta distribution. I've shipped apps end to end, including the App Store listing.

I use Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics, and I've worked with designers through Zeplin and documentation in Confluence. Working on analytics dashboards early on taught me how much data shapes product decisions.
Yes. Periplum ships in 6 locales via String Catalogs, the Bosch apps serve users across many countries and languages, and the B2B marketplace launched in 20 countries.
A Bachelor's Degree in Multimedia from Instituto Superior Miguel Torga (2015–2018).
Portuguese (native) and English (professional working proficiency).
Coimbra, Portugal.

I've shipped at scale (20 countries, four brands from one codebase), I've turned an app's reputation around (CustoJusto went up two stars to 4.5★), and I can take an app alone from first commit to App Store, as I did with Periplum. I care about the parts users don't see: API contracts, tests and hardware integration.

questions: Are you open to new opportunities?
Are you looking for a job?
Would you consider a new role?
topics.answer: Yes, I'm open to new opportunities. If you have a role in mind, email me at carlosanielrf@gmail.com.
Remote is my preference. Hybrid works too, if the office is within reasonable distance of Coimbra.

questions: What do you do in your free time?
What do you like outside work?
topics.answer: Gym, running, eating out, the beach, and hiking trails with my dog.
